note: A shorthand written after a longhand it covers now wins, as the later declaration: `css({ borderTopWidth: 2, borderWidth: 1 })` keeps only `border-width`, now that the sheet writes a longhand after its shorthands. The earlier longhand's atom is dropped in a css() object, styled objects (and their nested selectors), css() composition and Box props split by a spread, only when both are static and unconditional at the same selector, breakpoint, layer and style order; a conditional or dynamic value keeps both and the sheet order decides. Box props between two spreads have no written order, as the lint sorts them by name, so there the longhand still wins (`<Text backgroundClip='text' bg='linear-gradient(...)' />` keeps its gradient text). globalCss keeps every declaration in the order written. No new build errors
